newsitem.title: UK: Thatcher triggers best quotes of past 18 years.
newsitem.headline: Thatcher triggers best quotes of past 18 years.

text.p: The Conservative Party ruled Britain for 18 years, revolutionising almost every aspect of life -- from home ownership and the right to strike, to the sell-off of state industries like water and telephones.
Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher was the dominant force in British life for 11 years before being forced to stand down as Conservative Party leader in November 1990.
Following are some of the memorable political quotations encapsulating the mood of Britain during the past 18 years -
MARGARET THATCHER
"The Iron Lady." Name given to Thatcher by Soviet newspaper Red Star, January 1976.
"Where there is discord may we bring harmony...where there is despair may we bring hope." Thatcher, quoting St Francis of Assisi, on winning election in May 1979.
"There is no such thing as society; there are individual men and women and there are families." Thatcher, October 1987.
"She cannot see an institution without hitting it with her handbag." Conservative MP Julian Critchley on Thatcher, June 1982.
"I am extraordinarily patient, provided I get my own way in the end." Thatcher, April 1989.
"She has the eyes of Caligula but the mouth of Marilyn Monroe." French President Francois Mitterrand, November 1990
"It's a funny old world." Thatcher, addressing cabinet on last day in office, November 1990.
"The further you got from Britain, the more admired you found she was." Former Labour prime minister James Callaghan, December 1990
FALKLANDS WAR
"Rejoice, rejoice." Thatcher, on British troops recapturing island of South Georgia, April 1982.
"Gotcha!" Sun newspaper headline on sinking of Argentine cruiser Belgrano, May 1982.
EUROPE

"While the rest of Europe is marching to confront the new challenges, the prime minister is shuffling along in the gutter in the opposite direction, like an old bag lady muttering imprecations at anyone who catches her eye." Labour MP Denis Healey, February 1990
"If I sounded lukewarm about our commitment to enter the European Exchange Rate Mechanism it was because of a frog in my throat." John Major, then finance minister, March 1990.
"This is all a German racket designed to take over the whole of Europe." Conservative cabinet minister Nicholas Ridley on European monetary union, July 1990.
"No! No! No!" Thatcher, stressing her opposition to single European currency and control from Brussels, October 1990.

"It's rather like sending your opening batsmen to the crease...to find that their bats have been broken before the game by the team captain." Foreign Secretary Geoffrey Howe, using a cricketing metaphor on Thatcher's undermining of colleagues in European Union negotiations, November 1990.
"Game, set and match to Britain," Major, after he won opt-outs for Britain in negotiations for the Maastricht treaty in December 1991.
JOHN MAJOR
"I shan't be pulling the levers but I shall be a very good back-seat driver." Thatcher, on the election of Major, November 1990.
"We give the impression of being in office but not in power." Finance Minister Norman Lamont after being sacked, June 1993.

"Fifty years on from now, Britain will still be the country of long shadows on county cricket grounds, warm beer, invincible green suburbs, dog lovers and -- as George Orwell said -- old maids bicycling to Holy Communion through the morning mist." Major, April 1993.

"It is time to get back to basics; to self-discipline and respect for the law, to consideration for others, to accepting responsibility for yourself and your family, and not shuffling it off on the state." Major, October 1993.
LABOUR PARTY
"If Margaret Thatcher wins on Thursday, I warn you not to be ordinary, not to be young, not to fall ill and not to grow old." Labour leader Neil Kinnock, on eve of 1987 election.
"A dead or dying beast lying across a railway line and preventing other trains from getting through." Roy Jenkins, former Labour Party MP, May 1987.
"Last year I was Bambi, this year I am Stalin. From Disneyland to dictatorship in 12 short months". Labour leader Tony Blair, September 1995
ECONOMY
"You turn if you want to; the lady's not for turning" Thatcher, on speculation she might do a u-turn on economic policy, October 1980.
"I grew up in the Thirties with our unemployed father. He did not riot, he got on his bike and looked for work." Cabinet minister Norman Tebbit, October 1981.

"South Yorkshire is like a police state which you might be expected to see in Chile but not here." Miners leader Arthur Scargill, describing police baton and horse charges during year-long miners strike, May 1984

"First of all the Georgian silver goes, then all that nice furniture that used to be in the saloon. Then the Canalettos go." Former Conservative Prime Minister Harold McMillan on Conservative privatisation programme, November 1985.
"If the policy isn't hurting, it isn't working." John Major, October 1989.
"Unemployment is a price worth paying," Finance minister Norman Lamont, May 1991.
"Yes it hurt, yes it worked." Conservative Party poster, July 1996.
MISCELLANEOUS
"Today we were unlucky, but remember we have only to be lucky once." IRA statement after bombing Brighton hotel hosting Thatcher and her cabinet, October 1984.
"Gentlemen, I think we had better move to another room," Major to cabinet after IRA mortar landed close to 10 Downing Street, February 1991.
"We have become a grandmother." Thatcher, March 1989
